newsitem.title: USA: US aluminum and zinc premiums firm, nickel wobbles.
newsitem.headline: US aluminum and zinc premiums firm, nickel wobbles.

text.p: Aluminum and zinc premiums in the United States remained firm, but nickel has wobbled following the U.S. Mint tender result last week, traders said.

Traders with aluminum metal they can deliver promptly were still able to get about 6.5 cents per pound premiums over LME cash, but some dealers doubted if the recent high of 7.0 cents was still easily obtainable except in very specific circumstances.
"Some of the edge seems to be coming off it," one dealer said. "Metal is moving again now that the floods have crested and things have begun to open up again."
Large parcels of metal had been trapped on barges on the flooded Ohio river last week.
Traders said more Russian A7E metal was also arriving at U.S. southern ports, a combination of sold and unsold metal, which would take further upward pressure off premiums.
Zinc premiums remain firm as well, with a good number of bidders in Wednesday's 2,828-tonne award of U.S. Stockpile metal.
"I think we are anticipating LME zinc stocks will continue to come down, unless the Chinese put on some material," a producer agent said.
He was skeptical of rumors that the Chinese were heavily short on LME but will put metal into warehouses to spoof the market down.
U.S. zinc premiums were still a firm 5.50 to 6.00 cents per pound over LME cash, underpinned by last week's U.S. Mint tender at similar levels.
Nickel premiums have softened, dragged down by the winning bids in last week's Mint tender, traders said. Premiums were quoted at 9 to 11 cents per pound over LME cash, down from 10 to 14 cents.
The tin market remained fairly quiet with premiums remaining soft with plenty of low lead material still available, traders said.
Low lead tin from Minsur's new smelter in Peru was available in the U.S., helping to move low lead premiums closer in line with traditionally cheaper Grade A metal, traders said.
The scrap market was also fairly subdued as many players were in Las Vegas to attend the Institute of Scrap Recycling Industries conference.

Aluminum alloy prices were still in the 77 to 78 cents per pound range for A380 alloy, but due to weakness creeping into the scrap market on the back of lower LME prices, 78 cents will be harder to achieve as March drew to a close, smelter officials said.
